main represents coherent, tested, documented work.
Normal changes reach main through a pull request and required checks.
One task maps to one temporary branch and one active owner.
Pull requests use squash merge and merged branches are deleted.
The same task branch is edited simultaneously on multiple machines.
A conflict is resolved deliberately and all affected checks are rerun.
Force pushes or deletion of main are allowed.
Safety, invariants, frozen configuration, and study release tags receive human approval.
An agent reads the canonical instruction chain before editing.
An agent inspects PROJECT_STATE.json and its assigned atomic-step row before work.
An agent declares task, branch, owner, scope, claimed paths, and stop conditions.
An agent changes unrelated files merely to clean up the repository.
An agent invents values for unresolved D-01 through D-18 decisions.
An invariant or authority conflict becomes a recorded blocker for human resolution.
Agents preserve user changes and avoid destructive Git operations.
Interface, schema, configuration, or observable behavior changes update tests and documentation in the same pull request.
Work is marked done without required evidence.
Agents record commands and checks run, results, and evidence paths.
An agent merges or releases its own work without required human authority.
Two agents own the same task or branch concurrently.
Parallel agents use separate worktrees and non-overlapping module scopes.
A handoff records completed work, remaining work, changed files, tests, risks, blockers, and next eligible step.
Trello and GitHub Issues are coordination mirrors; repository plan, events, evidence, and decisions remain canonical.
The immutable workbook is normalized into a versioned task catalog with stable IDs.
Progress changes are append-only events with unique IDs and actor, time, branch, transition, and evidence fields.
PROJECT_STATE.json is generated deterministically from the task catalog and events.
Agents hand-edit generated PROJECT_STATE.json after the reducer exists.
Task transitions follow the documented state machine and invalid transitions fail.
G0 through G8 are hard gates and require explicit evidence-backed pass events.
Completing tasks automatically passes a gate.
The current step is chosen deterministically from active, verification-pending, ready, or blocked work in sequence order.
Divergent event chains for one task fail reduction and require reconciliation.
Done or passed states carry evidence that can be resolved in Git, CI, or approved lab records.
